subtitle: See how the purpose of Minnesota’s Olmstead Plan connects with distinct contributions across agencies, goals people choose for themselves and evidence of what remains to be done.
scope: For colleagues considering how work connected with DHS contributes to Minnesota’s Olmstead Plan. Six original practice lessons distinguish the actual plan’s cross-agency purpose from an invented planning exercise, actual service decisions and a proposed plan update. This course makes no individual legal, eligibility or service determination and assigns no real agency goal, contact, reporting deadline or resource commitment. Actual current direction, professional responsibilities, policy tools, appropriate information use and decision authority remain. Participation in this learning is voluntary. The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads the program and provides guidance, knowledge and feedback while staff carry their own equity work. Native American and Tribal-specific matters go to the appropriate office within ADSA (Aging and Disability Services Administration).
introTranscript: A plan can connect agencies around people’s choices while each agency retains particular responsibilities. Begin with the purpose and public decision structure of Minnesota’s Olmstead Plan. Then follow an invented proposal from a person’s chosen contribution through place, timing and participation questions, a complete task map, personally learned meanings of care, alternative approaches and an actual practice exchange. Examine what the exchange improved and what it did not establish. You can learn through the full an example or retain a private insight without providing a real service record or creating an agency assignment.

lessons.title: Recognize the shared purpose and the actual plan structure
lessons.summary: Locate the connection between community choice and cross-agency work while keeping plan status and decision roles clear.
lessons.objective: Describe the Minnesota plan’s cross-agency purpose in relation to community choice.
objectives: Describe the Minnesota plan’s cross-agency purpose in relation to community choice.
Distinguish the public plan structure from one team’s invented learning proposal.
Identify why a draft plan should not be presented as adopted direction.
takeaways: A plan can connect different responsibilities around community participation.
A team’s proposal is not the whole plan or an individual service determination.
Use the current official source to distinguish proposals from adopted direction.
lessons.statement: Connect the work with people’s choices while keeping the plan’s actual status and responsibilities clear.

image.caption: Three people sit around a table with open laptops and notebooks; one person uses a wheelchair, and a whiteboard is visible.

intro.heading: A shared purpose needs more than a shared title
intro.body:
Minnesota’s Olmstead Plan connects state-agency work with people with disabilities living full, integrated lives in communities they choose. Its public description includes choice and person-centered planning alongside subjects such as housing, education, employment and transportation. These connections matter because a person’s community purpose may encounter more than one system. A completed activity within one office does not by itself show what that person can actually do.

The official structure distinguishes the Subcabinet’s direction from the Leadership Forum’s recommendations. The Olmstead Implementation Office helps bring public and agency contributions into the planning process. A colleague can learn from that structure without assuming membership, assigning another agency’s duties or treating an ordinary meeting as a plan decision. Actual current roles and materials should be consulted when taking real work forward.

The official update page identifies the next plan as a draft available for public review. A draft can be useful for understanding proposed direction, but its presence on an official website is not proof that all proposed goals have been adopted. This course does not select a numeric target, reporting calendar or proposed new workgroup as operative. A real task needs its applicable current direction rather than the most recent-looking document alone.

Olin is a colleague preparing an educational planning note. Its entire starting claim is: “Our three completed agency activities show that Adin can participate in the community as chosen. The next plan’s proposed directions are already our approved assignments.” Neither sentence is supported by the supplied beginning. There are no descriptions of the three activities, actual participation or adopted assignments. The note joins a hopeful purpose to results and authority it has not established.

The learning question is more useful when separated from that claim: what does Adin want to do, which contributions could matter and what is known about their connection? This question respects the shared purpose without deciding Adin’s rights or services. Privately identify the two unsupported moves, or reflect on a familiar assumption that an official-looking proposal must already govern your work. You do not need an actual plan responsibility or another person’s history to make that distinction.

inThisLesson: Distinguish direction, recommendations and ordinary proposals.
lessons.keyStatement: The Minnesota plan connects agency work with community choice; the example establishes neither Adin’s participation nor adopted assignments.

flashcards.back: Minnesota’s cross-agency plan supporting full, integrated community lives and choice for people with disabilities; its actual current direction is distinct from this learning fiction.
The public structure that directs plan work; an ordinary practice team does not become it.
The state-staff forum making recommendations to the Subcabinet, distinct from an individual team’s proposal.
A proposal under consideration, which should not be represented as adopted merely because it appears in an official source.
A particular activity linked with other relevant responsibilities and the person’s purpose, rather than a promise that one activity settles everything.
A question about what actually changed for people, distinct from counting activities or completing a planning note.

accordion.heading: Keep purpose, structure and status connected

items.title: Community choice gives the work its reason
items.body: A completed document can matter, yet the plan’s purpose concerns people’s lives and choices. In the original note, there is no account of Adin’s chosen activity or what was possible. Begin by asking about that purpose rather than declaring an outcome from unspecified office activity.

items.title: Recommendations and direction are distinct contributions
items.body: The official structure gives recommendations a place without making them identical to direction. Olin’s learning note has neither role. In actual work, identifying the responsible decision structure helps a colleague contribute without inventing authority or treating every proposal as a commitment.

items.title: A current draft remains a proposal
items.body: The update page explicitly presents the next plan as a draft. Its ideas can inform learning while current actual responsibilities remain to be identified. A newer title or an official file does not itself establish adoption, and this course invents no implementation deadline from that appearance.

tabs.heading: Compare ways to read the starting note

tabs.label: Count activity as participation
tabs.body: This reading treats three unspecified completed activities as proof of Adin’s chosen community involvement. It skips the person’s purpose and actual conditions. The activities may later matter, but their number supplies no evidence that participation occurred or fit what Adin wanted.

tabs.label: Treat a draft as an approved assignment
tabs.body: This reading converts proposed direction into an operative responsibility without evidence of adoption or an actual assignment. It could send collaborators toward an unsupported target. Keep the official draft’s status visible and consult the applicable direction before taking real work forward.

tabs.label: Connect purpose with roles and current status
tabs.body: This reading retains the potential usefulness of a cross-agency plan while identifying what the note has not established. It makes room for Adin’s own purpose, distinct contributions and actual plan direction. Those inquiries can improve the note without manufacturing a service decision or outcome.

check.question: What can Olin reasonably say at the beginning?
check.correct: The plan offers a cross-agency purpose connected with community choice, while this note has not established Adin’s participation or adopted assignments from the draft.
wrong: Three completed activities automatically prove Adin’s chosen participation.
Every proposed direction in a posted draft is already an approved assignment.
Distinct agency roles mean the plan cannot have a shared community purpose.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. This keeps the plan’s purpose and actual status distinct from the unsupported practice result.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Counting unspecified activities proves no chosen participation. A posted draft does not automatically create approved assignments. Distinct responsibilities can still connect around a shared purpose; identify their contribution and applicable direction rather than erasing the connection.

sorting.heading: Separate shared purpose, official distinction and unsupported result

Ask how contributions across systems relate to that purpose.
Recommendations are distinct from Subcabinet direction.
The update page describes the next plan as a draft.
Three unspecified activities prove Adin’s participation.

scenario.prompt: What is the most useful first correction?
options: Retain the plan’s purpose while identifying the person’s goal, actual contributions and applicable direction as questions to examine.

responses: This gives the learning a real purpose without inventing outcome or authority.
The number supplies no account of what Adin wanted or could do.

lessons.transfer: Privately locate the unsupported activity-to-outcome and draft-to-assignment moves, or examine a familiar meaning of official without a real plan record.

move.control: You can keep purpose, evidence and actual direction distinct.
move.failure: A shared title becomes proof of participation or adopted responsibility.

lessons.title: Map the chosen purpose and connected questions
lessons.summary: Read a person’s stated contribution and connect place, timing and participation questions without creating a service promise.
lessons.objective: Identify Adin’s stated purpose without substituting a preset activity.
objectives: Identify Adin’s stated purpose without substituting a preset activity.
Explain how distinct practical questions can connect around that purpose.
Describe a task map that leaves actual availability, authority and arrangements open.
takeaways: Begin with the purpose the person actually supplies.
Connected questions need distinct responsibilities rather than one enlarged office promise.
A useful map identifies practical unknowns as well as possible contributions.
lessons.statement: Map what matters to the chosen purpose without pretending the map delivers it.

image.caption: Three people sit around a table with open laptops and notebooks; one person uses a wheelchair, and a whiteboard is visible.

intro.heading: Read Adin’s purpose before counting activity
intro.body:
Adin’s full practice account is: “I want to contribute a short description of how I repair wooden stools at a neighborhood repair gathering. I want to choose the words and decide whether to read them myself. I am asking what would make that particular contribution workable, rather than asking someone to choose a special activity for me.” The account names a purpose, a contribution and two choices. It establishes no gathering availability, transport arrangement, employment goal, diagnosis or service eligibility.

Olin now proposes examining three connected questions. What is known about the proposed place and how it would be used? What timing or travel questions would need examination? How can Adin’s chosen words and decision about reading them remain part of the plan? These are invented learning questions, not assigned goals from Minnesota’s plan or a complete assessment of Adin’s needs. They make the shared purpose concrete while leaving room for another relevant question.

Lysa and Bren are invented collaborators from different planning areas. Lysa offers to describe the proposed place information available in the example; Bren offers to examine the wording of timing questions. Neither offer confirms a room, transport service or funding. Olin’s own proposed contribution is to connect those questions with Adin’s purpose and show what remains unanswered. This is a planning role rather than authority to decide every system involved.

The complete proposed map reads: “Purpose: Adin wants a chosen stool-repair contribution, with chosen words and a decision about reading them. Place question: ask what the proposed gathering setting requires and what is actually available. Timing question: ask which timing and travel matters need clarification, without treating a question as a ride offer. Participation question: ask what contribution method Adin wants to consider and which practical arrangements remain open.” A map can make dependencies visible without turning possibility into delivery.

The official plan’s range of subjects helps explain why related systems may matter in a community life. It does not require this particular map or determine that every subject applies to Adin. Privately trace the purpose through the four sentences. You can retain an intrinsic insight about how quickly a familiar activity can replace someone’s own purpose, without creating a real service plan or asking a person to disclose more than they chose.

inThisLesson: Locate place, timing and contribution questions.
Read the complete four-sentence proposed map.
lessons.keyStatement: The map connects practical questions with Adin’s chosen contribution, while actual setting, travel, method and responsible arrangements remain to be examined.

items.title: A stated purpose is more precise than a category
items.body: Calling the goal community participation would miss the chosen repair description and choice about reading it. Adin supplies those details, so the map can retain them. Their importance does not require a diagnosis, a full biography or proof that every other person would want the same contribution.

items.title: A dependency explains why contributors may connect
items.body: A workable gathering could involve place, time and contribution method together. A description of one part might affect another inquiry, but no part automatically settles the rest. Mapping that connection helps Olin see where useful knowledge could move without transferring every decision to one collaborator.

items.title: A question is distinct from a resource offer
items.body: Bren’s timing-question offer establishes no vehicle or trip. Lysa’s place-description offer establishes no room reservation. The map remains worthwhile when those limits are explicit: it organizes what should be examined rather than advertise resources the collaborators have not supplied.

tabs.label: Replace the purpose with a preset event
tabs.body: This map might show a completed activity yet lose Adin’s chosen content and contribution method. The actual account gives a reason to question that substitution. Retaining the person’s purpose makes the map more relevant without promising every proposed arrangement can be delivered.

tabs.label: Give one collaborator every responsibility
tabs.body: This map hides the limits of Lysa’s and Bren’s offers and Olin’s role. It could turn a useful connection into an unsupported service promise. Distinct contributions can be coordinated while actual decision, availability and information responsibilities remain where they belong.

tabs.label: Connect the purpose with particular open questions
tabs.body: This map makes the shared task recognizable: chosen contribution, setting, timing and method. It keeps each offer bounded and allows missing information to guide the next inquiry. Its result is clearer planning, with actual access and participation still unknown.

check.question: What does the proposed map establish?
check.correct: A connection between Adin’s chosen contribution and particular place, timing and method questions, with collaborator offers and actual arrangements still distinct.
wrong: Bren’s offer to examine a timing question confirms a transport service.
Lysa’s description offer reserves the gathering place.
The map allows Olin to replace Adin’s chosen contribution with any completed activity.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. It keeps the purpose central and names practical questions without supplying resources or overriding the person’s choice.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A timing-question offer is not a ride offer. A place-description offer reserves nothing. The map’s purpose is to retain Adin’s particular contribution and choices, not justify any substituted activity; recognize clearer inquiry while leaving actual arrangements open.

sorting.heading: Separate stated purpose, proposed inquiry and enlarged offer

items.text: Adin wants to contribute a stool-repair description.
Adin wants chosen words and a choice about reading them.
Ask which setting arrangements would matter.
Ask which timing and travel questions need clarification.
Bren has promised a vehicle by examining wording.
Lysa has reserved a place by offering a description.

scenario.prompt: How should Olin represent the offers?

As permission to substitute any completed event for the chosen contribution.

move.control: You can make connected questions visible while retaining choice and actual responsibilities.
move.failure: A useful inquiry becomes a resource promise or a replacement purpose.

lessons.title: Receive the meanings behind preparation and invitation
lessons.summary: Understand two original personal accounts of care and change a proposal without using them to predict agencies or disability preferences.
lessons.objective: Explain Ione’s and Dev’s different learned meanings of care.
objectives: Explain Ione’s and Dev’s different learned meanings of care.
Widen Olin’s obstruction and neglect judgments through the supplied accounts.
Connect the wider frame with a complete invitation that keeps contribution and choice open.
takeaways: Preparation and early inquiry can express different personally learned purposes.
Receiving a meaning can widen a judgment without making it a group trait.
A changed invitation should make the connection visible in actual words.
lessons.statement: Hear what a familiar approach protects before deciding what another approach means.

image.caption: Three people sit around a table with open laptops and notebooks; one person uses a wheelchair, and a whiteboard is visible.

intro.heading: Two ways care became recognizable
intro.body:
A separate original voluntary community-display encounter gives Olin a chance to examine the meaning of preparation. Ione says: “In my chosen shared-kitchen circle, preparing a usable place before inviting a contribution was a way to show that the person’s effort mattered. I do not want an invitation to suggest that someone must discover all the missing practical work alone.” Dev says: “In my chosen story circle, asking about someone’s purpose before preparing the setting was a way to show that their account could shape it. A prepared place could still leave no room for what they wanted to do.” These are personally supplied learned meanings, not claims about national groups, disability or all circles.

Olin initially treats Ione’s preparation question as obstruction and Dev’s early invitation as neglect of practical work. Each judgment takes Olin’s familiar order as the only responsible one. Ione’s account makes effort and dependable preparation visible. Dev’s makes purpose and influence visible. Receiving both changes the frame: the tension concerns how care becomes recognizable, rather than proving one person opposes participation or refuses preparation.

Neither account resolves the availability questions in Adin’s map or predicts Lysa’s and Bren’s motives. Understanding a meaning is different from completing an arrangement. Olin can preserve the useful tension by asking about a chosen purpose early, showing actual preparation limits and inviting a particular contribution to the practical question. A common invitation need not pretend the two sequences are identical.

Olin’s complete changed invitation is: “The proposed display would begin with the purpose you want your contribution to serve. We can describe the preparation already considered and the practical questions still open, rather than asking you to carry unseen work. Would you prefer to begin with a chosen account, a question about preparation, or another starting point? Your response would inform the proposal without committing you to participating or proving the setting is ready.” The words connect Dev’s influence purpose with Ione’s care for effort, while actual preparation and response remain unperformed.

Council of Europe educational discussion helps distinguish personally enacted meanings, contextual interpretation and a response changed through wider understanding. It does not provide a formula that diagnoses the people or guarantees the invitation’s result. Privately compare Olin’s first judgments and the new offer. An intrinsic understanding of care, purpose or preparation is worthwhile without a real agency project, disclosure of your history or another person’s acceptance.

inThisLesson: Examine the initial obstruction and neglect judgments.
Keep practical outcomes and agency motives distinct.
lessons.keyStatement: Ione’s care for effort and Dev’s care for purpose widen Olin’s frame and change the invitation, without proving readiness, acceptance or anyone else’s preference.

accordion.heading: Connect meaning with the changed response

items.title: Preparation can recognize a contribution’s effort
items.body: Ione’s shared-kitchen account explains why a practical question matters before someone is asked to contribute. Olin can now hear responsibility rather than only obstruction. That meaning does not establish an available place or make Ione the authority on everyone’s needs; it supplies a reason to describe what is prepared and what remains.

items.title: Early inquiry can protect influence
items.body: Dev’s story-circle account explains why a fully prepared setting can still exclude a person’s chosen purpose. Olin can hear influence rather than only neglect. Asking early does not solve practical work, but it can change what that work is trying to make possible rather than invite a person only after their role is fixed.

items.title: The invitation receives both purposes without merging them
items.body: The revised words begin with purpose, make considered preparation and unknowns visible, and offer different starting points. This is a contextual response to the meanings actually given. It accepts no contribution, establishes no readiness and predicts no agency’s motives; a useful change can retain that honest limit.

tabs.label: Keep obstruction and neglect as final explanations
tabs.body: This frame treats Olin’s initial judgments as facts even after the people explain different care purposes. It would hide effort and influence inside negative labels. Receiving those meanings supports a wider interpretation without requiring agreement that either sequence works in every setting.

tabs.label: Assign the two meanings to all agencies or disabled people
tabs.body: This frame extends chosen personal accounts to people who supplied no such meaning. It would replace inquiry with a profile and could distort Adin’s actual words. The encounter helps Olin learn, but Lysa, Bren and Adin retain their own purposes and responsibilities.

tabs.label: Offer purpose inquiry with visible preparation limits
tabs.body: This frame follows both care meanings into the full four-sentence invitation. It makes a chosen beginning possible while explaining the practical work still open. The actual invitation can be examined as a proposal without certifying participation or using a changed interpretation as a service outcome.

check.question: Which account follows the received meanings?
check.correct: Ione’s effort and Dev’s influence purposes widen Olin’s judgments and inform a full choice-based invitation, while readiness, acceptance and other people’s preferences remain open.
wrong: Ione’s preparation question proves she opposes community participation.
Dev’s account proves all disabled people prefer early storytelling.
The changed invitation confirms every practical arrangement is ready.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The encounter connects personal meaning, wider interpretation and changed words while keeping later outcomes and other people’s choices distinct.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Ione explains care for effort rather than opposition. Dev gives a chosen personal purpose, not a disability preference rule. The new words explicitly retain practical questions; an improved invitation confirms no readiness. Keep the meaning learning without enlarging its reach or result.

sorting.heading: Separate received meaning, changed words and unsupported inference

items.text: Ione connects usable preparation with respect for a person’s effort.
Dev connects early purpose inquiry with meaningful influence.
The invitation names considered preparation and open practical work.
The invitation offers a chosen account or preparation question as a start.
All agency partners share Dev’s exact preference.
The wider interpretation proves the gathering setting is ready.

scenario.prompt: What should Olin retain from the encounter?
options: A prediction that every agency shares one person’s preferred sequence.
A finding that Adin’s community participation is complete.
The received care purposes and changed contextual invitation, leaving other people’s choices and practical results open.
responses: Chosen meanings supply no agency profile.
This separate encounter establishes no participation result for Adin.
This preserves real meaning learning and a concrete response without manufacturing an outcome.

lessons.transfer: Privately compare care as dependable preparation and care as purpose influence, or retain an intrinsic insight without a biography or accepted contribution.

move.control: You can widen an interpretation through the purpose someone actually supplies.
move.failure: A care difference becomes a character verdict, disability profile or readiness claim.

lessons.title: Read the evidence of each connection
lessons.summary: Distinguish a completed description, an unanswered question and a person’s stated choice from proof of participation.
lessons.objective: Classify the three supplied planning entries by what each establishes.
objectives: Classify the three supplied planning entries by what each establishes.
Explain why an unanswered practical question is neither success nor failure evidence.
Write a whole evidence account that keeps the person’s purpose connected with remaining work.
takeaways: A completed description can be useful without establishing availability.
A question still open should remain visible rather than interpreted as satisfaction or refusal.
A person’s stated choice deserves its own account rather than disappearance inside activity counts.
lessons.statement: Describe what each contribution actually shows before claiming what changed for the person.

intro.heading: Three entries tell different parts of the story
intro.body:
Olin receives this entire practice planning record. Entry one, from Lysa: “I have described the proposed gathering space in this educational example. It includes a table where a repair description might be presented. I have not confirmed that a gathering is available, that this table arrangement fits Adin, or that anyone has agreed to prepare it.” Entry two, from Bren: “I have written the question: which timing or travel matters would need clarification for the proposed contribution? No answer or travel offer is recorded.” Entry three, from Adin: “I still want to choose my description and decide whether to read it myself. I have not tried a gathering arrangement in this example.” These are the full three entries, not summaries of undisclosed case records.

The first entry establishes a description and explicit practical limits. The second establishes a formulated question with no answer or offer. The third retains Adin’s own purpose and a lack of actual trial. Counting three entries as three completed participation outcomes would erase the differences. Discarding all three because no gathering occurred would erase useful preparation and the person’s own account.

A good evidence account connects the states without making a causal story it cannot support. The proposed place might matter to the contribution, but actual fit and availability remain unknown. Timing and travel remain questions, not proved barriers or provided support. Adin’s stated choices remain relevant, and there is no observed participation to evaluate. Missing conditions identify further inquiry without turning an unanswered question into refusal, inability or satisfaction.

Olin writes the whole account: “A place description and a timing question have been prepared. The description does not confirm availability or fit, and the timing question has no answer or travel offer. Adin retains chosen words and a choice about reading, with no trial of the arrangement supplied. The record supports connected planning questions and a stated purpose, not a finding that community participation has occurred or failed.” This preserves information collaborators can use without inventing an official plan metric or claiming the exercise meets an adopted target.

The official documents library separates plans, reports and workplans. Reading the right material matters when moving from this learning record to actual plan work. An exercise note is not a required public report, a person-centered service plan or a release determination for real records. Privately compare the entries with Olin’s four-sentence account. You may instead retain an intrinsic understanding of how useful partial work and honest unknowns can coexist, without collecting real personal information.

Locate the missing trial and arrangements.

lessons.keyStatement: The record supports useful descriptions, questions and choices, while actual availability, fit, travel and participation remain unknown rather than proved successful or failed.

accordion.heading: Read the connection without enlarging the result

items.title: The place description has a real but limited contribution
items.body: Lysa supplies a proposed feature and makes its limits explicit. That description can help formulate a fit question. It does not establish a reserved place, a suitable method or agreed preparation, so the account should recognize the description without using it as access proof.

items.title: An unanswered question creates an information gap
items.body: Bren supplies the exact question and says no answer or travel offer is recorded. The gap identifies what is not known. It does not explain why the answer is absent or establish a transportation barrier, a declined offer or satisfaction with an arrangement.

items.title: Adin’s stated choice is not an observed outcome
items.body: Adin’s account keeps chosen words and reading choice in the work. No actual trial is supplied, so participation cannot be called successful or unsuccessful. Keeping the choice visible makes the next inquiry more relevant without requiring a personal story or substituting a completed office task for experience.

tabs.heading: Compare accounts of the three entries

tabs.label: Three entries mean three participation successes
tabs.body: This account converts different planning states into the same outcome. It would hide Lysa’s explicit limits, Bren’s unanswered question and Adin’s untried arrangement. Counts may describe recorded entries, but their number alone does not establish community choice or participation.

tabs.label: No trial means every contribution failed
tabs.body: This account turns unknown actual use into a negative finding and loses the prepared description, question and stated purpose. The supplied work is useful for a next inquiry even though it does not prove a service result. An honest limit does not make the contribution worthless.

tabs.label: Retain each entry and its practical unknown
tabs.body: This account distinguishes useful partial work from the later experience it aims to support. It can show how descriptions, timing inquiry and chosen method connect. The four-sentence note remains a learning account, with actual report requirements and real information responsibilities separate.

check.question: Which conclusion is supported by the full record?
check.correct: A place description, unanswered timing question and stated contribution choices support further connected inquiry, with actual arrangements and participation still unknown.
wrong: Three entries prove three successful participation outcomes.
An unanswered timing question proves Adin has refused all travel help.
No trial proves the place description and Adin’s stated purpose have no value.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. This recognizes each supplied contribution and preserves the missing conditions as unknown.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Entry counts are not participation outcomes. Bren records no answer or offer, so refusal cannot be inferred. Lack of a trial does not erase a useful description or Adin’s chosen purpose; keep the concrete gains and missing actual experience together rather than invent success or failure.

sorting.heading: Separate supplied evidence, open condition and unsupported finding

items.text: Lysa has described a possible table feature.
Adin states chosen words and a choice about reading.
Actual gathering availability and fit remain unconfirmed.
The timing question has no recorded answer or travel offer.
Three entries prove chosen community participation occurred.
No answer proves Adin declined every possible arrangement.

scenario.prompt: How should the evidence be represented?
options: As useful connected planning information with each actual limit and missing condition visible.
As three successful outcomes because each entry is recorded.
As a proved refusal because no timing answer is supplied.
responses: This preserves useful work without turning activity or silence into an outcome.
The entries describe different states, not three participation results.
The record gives no reason for the absent answer and no offer to decline.

lessons.transfer: Privately compare the full entries with the evidence account, or examine how partial work can matter without a real report or personal record.

move.control: You can preserve what is known and what is missing in the same account.
move.failure: Activity counts or silence become invented participation results.

intro.heading: From a comparison to a performed exchange
intro.body:
Olin compares three complete planning approaches. Approach A is: “Report each finished entry as a separate success and add them together as Adin’s participation.” Approach B is: “Give Olin responsibility for providing every place, travel and contribution arrangement, regardless of actual authority.” Approach C is: “Keep Adin’s chosen contribution central; connect each supplied entry with its particular unanswered condition; seek relevant clarification through actual roles before claiming participation.” The approaches differ in what they would hide or retain, not in how impressive their labels sound.

A offers an easy report but turns descriptions and questions into an experience not supplied. B appears decisive but makes one colleague responsible for powers and resources the record does not give. C retains the useful work and practical connections. It does not guarantee an arrangement or prescribe a universal coordination routine; its reason is that the actual entries and purpose deserve a more accurate account.

The example now supplies a performed exchange. Olin asks: “Does the map distinguish your contribution from the practical conditions still open, and does it keep Adin’s chosen purpose recognizable?” Lysa replies: “Please keep the table as a described possibility rather than a confirmed place or fit. The next place question should ask what arrangement would need examination for the chosen contribution.” Bren replies: “Keep timing and travel as unanswered questions. My written question is not a ride offer.” Adin replies: “Keep my choice of words and whether I read them. I have not agreed to a gathering arrangement.” These exact replies guide a revision, not service approval.

Olin’s whole replacement map is: “Purpose: Adin wants a chosen stool-repair contribution, with chosen words and a choice about reading them. Place: a table possibility is described, while actual availability, fit and arrangement need examination through relevant responsibilities. Timing: timing and travel remain unanswered questions, with no ride offer supplied. Contribution method: Adin’s stated choices remain, with no agreed or tried gathering arrangement. Claim: this map supports connected planning questions rather than proof of successful or failed participation.” Each sentence follows the supplied exchange.

Actual DHS Equity Policy responsibilities remain separate. Staff continue their equity work and daily consideration, and qualifying formal proposals require the applicable agency analysis or scan toolkit, or a custom tool developed in consultation with the equity director. This original map does not substitute for those requirements, authorize service changes or become an official Olmstead reporting measure. The consultant leads the program and provides guidance and feedback while colleagues carry their work. Privately compare the alternatives and whole revision, or retain an intrinsic insight about responsible connection without a real case or formal submission.

lessons.keyStatement: Approach C and the performed replies support a purpose-linked map with honest practical limits, not a service arrangement, official outcome measure or substitute for required analysis.

items.title: Adding activities hides the missing connection
items.body: Approach A would count the entries but miss their different states and relationship with Adin’s purpose. The table is possible, timing is unanswered and contribution choice is stated. Those entries do not become participation when added; retain their practical meaning rather than make the report easier by changing the claim.

items.title: Enlarging a role does not supply its missing authority
items.body: Approach B gives Olin every arrangement without identifying an actual mandate or resource. This could conceal where coordination needs another responsibility. A colleague can connect questions and evidence without pretending the learning note grants every service or decision power.

items.title: The performed exchange supplies a reason for precise revision
items.body: Lysa distinguishes possibility from fit, Bren question from offer and Adin choice from agreement. The five-sentence replacement follows those corrections. Its gain is a clearer account of connected work; a better map still leaves actual current plan direction, resources and participation to their appropriate work.

tabs.heading: Compare the approaches and their implications

tabs.label: A: Count separate entries as a completed outcome
tabs.body: This approach makes a simple result look available by ignoring each entry’s limit. It could obscure exactly where participation remains unexamined. The record supports particular preparation, not Adin’s actual community experience, so the approach would sacrifice accuracy for a convenient success statement.

tabs.label: B: Make one colleague responsible for everything
tabs.body: This approach confuses coordination with all-system authority. It hides relevant roles and the missing real arrangements behind Olin’s name. A shared purpose can require connected contributions without transferring every resource, service or legal responsibility to the person drafting a note.

tabs.label: C: Connect purpose, evidence and open responsibilities
tabs.body: This approach retains useful preparation while keeping practical unknowns and the person’s choices attached. The actual exchange makes the revised map more specific. Its tradeoff is that it leaves a less tidy result with further work open, yet that honest account is more usable than manufactured completion.

check.question: Why does approach C fit the supplied record?
check.correct: It retains Adin’s purpose, each entry’s actual contribution and open conditions, allowing the exact replies to support a precise map without claiming an arrangement or replacing actual responsibilities.
wrong: Approach A is strongest because adding three entries always proves an outcome.
Approach B gives Olin real authority merely by putting every task under one name.
Approach C automatically completes the agency’s required equity analysis and all plan reporting.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The choice follows the actual evidence and gives a concrete reason for the replacement while keeping formal responsibilities separate.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Three entries do not prove an outcome. Naming Olin supplies no new authority or resource. The purpose-linked learning map replaces neither qualifying agency analysis nor actual plan reporting; recognize the performed clarification and accurate revision without enlarging their status.

sorting.heading: Separate comparison reason, performed clarification and invented completion

B would enlarge Olin’s role beyond supplied authority.

The voluntary map completes every required formal analysis.

lessons.title: Follow the connection through an honest closing
lessons.summary: Recognize a clearer map and a retained personal purpose while keeping real participation, current direction and future responsibilities open.
lessons.objective: Describe the three closing comments without enlarging their scope.
objectives: Describe the three closing comments without enlarging their scope.
Identify a fitting continuation question for the practical conditions still open.
Distinguish intrinsic learning and planning improvement from an actual community outcome or permanent competence.
takeaways: A more accurate map is a gain with a specific scope.
Follow-through concerns the actual unresolved connection rather than an invented success or failure.
Private learning about care and influence can remain meaningful without a service result.
lessons.statement: Close with what the work actually improved and the connection it still needs to examine.

intro.heading: A useful gain is not the whole outcome
intro.body:
The example closes with these complete comments. Lysa says: “The replacement now distinguishes the described table from a confirmed place or fit. Actual place arrangements remain to be examined.” Bren says: “The map no longer makes my timing question a ride offer. The question still has no answer.” Adin says: “My chosen words and choice about reading remain recognizable. I have not tried or agreed to a gathering arrangement.” Each comment supports a particular improvement and keeps a different practical condition open.

Olin writes the entire closing: “The starting note overstated participation and adopted assignments. The chosen purpose, three distinct entries and performed clarifications now support a map that keeps place, timing and contribution questions connected. The replies recognize particular distinctions rather than establish availability, travel or a workable gathering. Actual current plan direction, responsible arrangements and Adin’s experience remain to be examined before a participation claim.” This account recognizes progress without manufacturing a public plan result or implying that unanswered questions prove failure.

A fitting continuation would ask which actual responsibility can examine a relevant remaining condition and how the person’s chosen purpose would remain visible. The next step would depend on actual work, current plan direction and appropriate information use. The example accepts no agency assignment, deadline, resource promise or real case transfer. Maintaining a connected question is different from declaring every condition solved or adopting a new goal through a learning exercise.

The original Ione and Dev encounter offers another gain. Care for someone’s effort and care for their influence widened Olin’s obstruction and neglect judgments. The changed invitation made both purposes understandable while acceptance and preparation remained open. You may keep that intrinsic understanding privately; it needs no service outcome, agency report or public account to be worthwhile. It also predicts none of Adin’s, Lysa’s or Bren’s motives.

The plan’s cross-agency purpose remains concrete when colleagues connect their actual contributions to people’s chosen lives and ask what those contributions establish. Counting activity, merging authority and treating drafts as adopted direction can hide that work. This course supplies an educational example rather than an individual legal determination; actual legal application belongs with the responsible professional roles. Privately name one supported gain and one unresolved connection from the full fiction, or retain a meaningful insight about care and choice without certifying competence, disclosing a biography or claiming real participation.

inThisLesson: Value planning and intrinsic learning without an enlarged outcome.
lessons.keyStatement: The closing supports a clearer purpose-linked map and retained choices, with actual arrangements, participation and current direction still open; intrinsic meaning learning is a separate worthwhile gain.

accordion.heading: Recognize the gain and the next connection

items.title: The comments support different improvements
items.body: Lysa recognizes possibility versus confirmed place, Bren question versus offer and Adin retained choices versus an arrangement. These comments are concrete evidence about the map. They are not approval of services, evidence that every condition is satisfied or a collective conclusion from all people affected by Minnesota’s plan.

items.title: Continuation should follow the actual unresolved condition
items.body: The remaining questions concern place, timing, contribution arrangement and applicable direction. An actual continuation should locate the relevant responsibility and information rather than invent a new service commitment from the note. Keeping a question connected with the person’s purpose makes further work more relevant without predetermining its result.

items.title: Private meaning learning does not need an operational claim
items.body: Ione’s and Dev’s care purposes can change how you understand an invitation. Such self-understanding need not become a real agency task or public reflection. It should remain distinct from claims about participation, but its value is not erased because the practice gathering has not occurred.

tabs.label: Declare the whole plan and participation successful
tabs.body: This claim would turn three narrow comments into an outcome for Adin and Minnesota’s cross-agency work. The supplied record gives no gathering trial or all-plan evidence. Recognizing the clearer map does not require enlarging its scope into success for every contribution or person.

tabs.label: Declare all planning and learning worthless
tabs.body: This claim would turn unfinished practical work into total failure and lose the actual purpose, clarifications and accurate revision. The missing conditions matter, yet they do not erase what the comments establish. The intrinsic care insight can also remain worthwhile without an operational result.

tabs.label: Retain exact gains and actual unresolved connections
tabs.body: This claim follows the full closing comments and Olin’s account. It recognizes clearer planning and choices while asking how real work would examine the remaining conditions through applicable direction. The account can support a fitting continuation or private understanding without inventing a deadline, legal determination or competence certificate.

check.question: Which closing account is faithful to the example?
check.correct: The replies support clearer contribution distinctions and retained choices, with actual arrangements, current direction and participation open; the separate care insight can remain privately meaningful.
wrong: The three comments certify Adin’s participation and success of the whole Minnesota plan.
An unanswered timing question proves the collaboration and every contribution failed.
Private learning counts only if a real agency arrangement and public report follow.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The closing recognizes specific gains and unresolved practical work without erasing intrinsic learning or claiming an unsupported outcome.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The comments concern the map, not observed participation or the whole plan. A missing answer establishes no total failure. Private understanding can matter without a real arrangement or public report; keep actual operational claims distinct while recognizing meaningful learning and accurate planning.

sorting.heading: Separate closing gain, remaining connection and enlarged claim

items.text: Lysa recognizes a clearer distinction between description and confirmed place.
Adin recognizes chosen words and reading choice in the map.
Actual timing and travel questions remain unanswered.
Applicable current direction and responsible arrangements need examination in real work.
The comments certify success of every Minnesota plan goal.
Private understanding has no value without a public service outcome.

move.control: You can keep a gain’s scope attached to the contribution and unfinished work.
move.failure: A clearer map becomes universal success, total failure or a compulsory public account.

jobAid.title: Connect the purpose, contribution and remaining question
jobAid.subtitle: An optional planning and reflection aid using the whole example; actual Minnesota plan direction, legal application, service decisions and required tools remain distinct.
remember: A count of activities is not proof of a person’s chosen community participation. A draft is not an adopted assignment. Keep actual purpose, contributions, evidence and remaining conditions connected.

sections.heading: Locate the purpose and actual direction
items: Minnesota’s plan connects agency work with people’s chosen integrated community lives. Subcabinet direction, Leadership Forum recommendations and a learning proposal are distinct.
The current update page presents the next plan as a draft. This aid supplies no adopted numeric target, new workgroup or reporting deadline; use applicable current direction for real work.

sections.heading: Begin with the person’s supplied purpose
items: Adin wants a chosen stool-repair description, chosen words and a choice about reading them. The full account supplies no gathering, travel, service eligibility or diagnosis.
The four-sentence proposed map connects place, timing and contribution method with that purpose. Lysa’s description and Bren’s timing-question offers confirm no room, fit, ride or funding.

sections.heading: Receive meanings before judging the approach
items: Ione’s personally chosen shared-kitchen preparation protects effort; Dev’s story-circle early inquiry protects influence. These meanings widen Olin’s obstruction and neglect judgments.

The full invitation starts with purpose, makes considered preparation and unknowns visible and offers a chosen starting point. It establishes neither readiness nor acceptance, predicts no agency or disability preference and permits learning through private reflection.

sections.heading: Describe each entry’s actual evidence
items: Lysa describes a possible table with availability and fit unconfirmed; Bren records an unanswered timing question with no travel offer; Adin retains choices with no arrangement trial.

The whole four-sentence evidence account recognizes useful preparation and stated purpose while keeping participation unknown. Missing conditions are not refusal, inability, satisfaction or proof every contribution failed.

sections.heading: Choose through purpose, evidence and responsibilities
items: A counts separate entries as participation; B gives Olin unsupported all-system authority; C connects the purpose with each contribution and open condition. The performed replies support the whole five-sentence replacement map.

Actual staff equity work, daily consideration and qualifying DHS formal analysis or scan toolkit/custom-tool consultation with the equity director remain. This voluntary map is not a required report, service plan, individual legal decision or substitute for actual responsibilities. The consultant leads the program and provides guidance while staff carry their own work.

sections.heading: Close with the supported gain and next connection
items: The exact comments recognize clearer possibility/fit, question/offer and choice/arrangement distinctions. Olin’s closing retains actual arrangements, current direction and participation as open rather than declare whole-plan success or failure.

A real continuation needs relevant responsibilities and appropriate information; the example accepts no assignment or resource commitment. Private care-and-choice insight remains meaningful without a public outcome. Native American and Tribal-specific matters go to the appropriate office within ADSA (Aging and Disability Services Administration).
